message.text:
This is asking about persistent entity types defined in the data layer and which ones are referenced most from outside the data layer.

The data layer is likely the `store/` package. I need to:
1. Find all persistent entity types (structs) defined in store/
2. Count how many packages outside store/ reference each type
3. Rank the top two

Let me search for type definitions in the store package and count their references in other packages.
I'll identify persistent entity types defined in the store layer and count their references from other packages.
Let me continue and get all entity types, then count their references from outside the store package:

args.command: grep "^type.*struct" /bench/repo/store/*.go | grep -v test | grep -v "^/bench/repo/store/.*:/.*Find\|^/bench/repo/store/.*:/.*Update\|^/bench/repo/store/.*:/.*Delete" | awk -F: '{print $2}' | awk '{print $2}' | sort

message.text: Good! Now let me count references to the main entity types from outside the store package. Let me focus on the main persistent entity types (capitalized, non-operation types):

args.command: for type in "Memo" "User" "Attachment" "Reaction" "MemoShare" "Inbox" "UserIdentity" "MemoRelation" "IdentityProvider"; do count=$(grep -rn "store\.$type\|\\*store\\.$type" /bench/repo --include="*.go" | grep -v "^/bench/repo/store" | grep -v test | wc -l); echo "$type: $count"; done

message.text: Excellent! User has 78 references and Memo has 69. Let me verify these numbers are coming from outside the store package and count which packages reference them:

args.command: echo "=== store.User references by package ==="; grep -rn "store\.User\|\*store\.User" /bench/repo --include="*.go" | grep -v "^/bench/repo/store" | grep -v test | cut -d/ -f1-5 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -15

echo "=== store.Memo references by package ==="; grep -rn "store\.Memo\|\*store\.Memo" /bench/repo --include="*.go" | grep -v "^/bench/repo/store" | grep -v test | cut -d/ -f1-5 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -15

message.text: Good! Let me get more granular package counts for these two types:

args.command: echo "=== store.User references by package (detailed) ==="; grep -rn "store\.User\|\*store\.User" /bench/repo --include="*.go" | grep -v "^/bench/repo/store" | grep -v test | cut -d: -f1 | sed 's|/bench/repo/||' | sed 's|/[^/]*\.go||' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

message.text:
Perfect! Now I can count the number of distinct packages that reference each type:

- **User**: Referenced from 6 packages (server/router/api/v1, proto/gen/store, server/auth, server/notification, server/router/rss, server/router/fileserver) with ~78 references
- **Memo**: Referenced from 6 packages (server/router/api/v1, server/notification, proto/gen/store, server/runner/memopayload, server/router/rss, server/router/fileserver) with ~69 references

Both are referenced from 6 packages. Let me verify the exact counts and also check if there are any other entity types that might be close:

args.command: for type in "User" "Memo" "Attachment" "Inbox" "MemoRelation"; do packages=$(grep -rn "store\.$type\|\*store\.$type" /bench/repo --include="*.go" | grep -v "^/bench/repo/store" | grep -v test | cut -d: -f1 | sed 's|/bench/repo/||' | sed 's|/[^/]*\.go||' | sort -u | wc -l); total=$(grep -rn "store\.$type\|\*store\.$type" /bench/repo --include="*.go" | grep -v "^/bench/repo/store" | grep -v test | wc -l); echo "$type: $packages packages, $total refs"; done
